hints: Focus on the functional group first, the name ends in -al so you are dealing with an aldehyde with its own characteristic tests.
Recall that both 2,4-DNPH and Tollens' reagent are classic positive tests for aldehydes, so check what those two do.
For the iodine test, ask yourself if this bulky aldehyde contains the special group needed for the iodoform reaction, a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ group or $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$.
walkthrough:
**Identify the molecule**

Great start, the suffix -anal tells us this is an aldehyde. Let's draw it out.

$$\text{OHC-C(CH}_3)_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_3$$
This is 2,2,4-trimethylpentanal, a branched aldehyde with no $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ group.

**Test 1 with 2,4-DNPH**

2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine reacts with the C=O of all aldehydes and ketones to give an orange precipitate. Since we have an aldehyde, this test is positive.

**Test 2 with Tollens' reagent**

Tollens' reagent, $\text{[Ag(NH}_3)_2]^+$, is a mild oxidising agent that oxidises aldehydes to carboxylic acids but does not oxidise ketones.

$$\text{R-CHO + 2[Ag(NH}_3)_2]^+ + 3OH^- \rightarrow \text{R-COO}^- + 2\text{Ag} + 4\text{NH}_3 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Our compound is an aldehyde, so we get the silver mirror. This test is positive.

**Test 3 with alkaline aqueous iodine**

This is the iodoform test. It is only positive for methyl ketones, $\text{CH}_3\text{COR}$, and for ethanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, and for alcohols of type $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$.
Our aldehyde has a $\text{-C(CH}_3)_2\text{-}$ next to the $\text{-CHO}$ group, not a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ group, so no yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate forms. This test is negative.

**Conclude the combination**

Only 1 and 2 react. That corresponds to 1 and 2 only.

options.A: Incorrect. This option claims 1, 2 and 3 all react. While 1 and 2 are correct, 3 is wrong because 2,2,4-trimethylpentanal lacks the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ structure needed for the triiodomethane (iodoform) reaction.
options.B: Correct. As an aldehyde it gives an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH (1) and a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent (2), but it cannot give iodoform with alkaline aqueous iodine (3) because it is not ethanal and has no methyl ketone group.
options.C: Incorrect. This option claims 2 and 3 only. It correctly includes Tollens' but wrongly includes alkaline iodine and wrongly leaves out 2,4-DNPH, which all aldehydes react with.
options.D: Incorrect. This option claims 1 only. It is true that 2,4-DNPH reacts, but it misses that Tollens' reagent also oxidises this aldehyde. Students choosing this may have confused aldehydes with ketones for Tollens' test.
